CBSA.CICSBSA.ABNDFILE.recovery_why: etc/install/base/installjcl/BANK.csd: DEFINE FILE(ABNDFILE) ... RECOVERY(NONE) -- the abend log a backout must not undo

scenarios.name: not-on-file
scenarios.why: customer 5 has an account but no CUSTOMER record: INQCUST fails, COMM-DEL-SUCCESS 'N' with INQCUST's fail code, RETURN; nothing deleted

scenarios.name: customer-zero
scenarios.why: customer 0000000000: INQCUST resolves it to the last customer, the READ of key 0000000000 is NOTFND: the program's own failure path

scenarios.name: read-sysiderr-retried

faults.why: 53 on DELCUS's READ UPDATE (the 3rd READ of CUSTOMER in the task: INQCUST, INQACCCU's INQCUST, DELCUS)

scenarios.why: DELCUS's READ FOR UPDATE gets SYSIDERR once: DELAY 3 seconds (a task takes no time, X4), READ again, then the deletion goes on

scenarios.name: delete-ioerr
scenarios.why: the DELETE of the CUSTOMER record fails with IOERR: the program's failure path

notes: CBSA's delete-customer service (DELCUS, LINKed by BNK1DCS with the DELCUS copybook's COMMAREA). It LINKs INQCUST (the customer must exist: 'N' and INQCUST's fail code otherwise), lists the customer's accounts through INQACCCU (SYNCONRETURN), LINKs DELACC for each (ACCOUNT row deleted, PROCTRAN 'ODA' row written, as in cbsa-delacc), then READs the CUSTOMER record FOR UPDATE and DELETEs it, retrying on SYSIDERR (DELAY FOR SECONDS(3), no time passes in a task, oracle_assumptions.md X4). ACCOUNT, PROCTRAN, CUSTOMER and ABNDFILE are compared after every scenario. Data: seed.sql is cbsa-delacc's and customer.txt is cbsa-bnk1cca's (SYNTHETIC). Not reached: failure branches no fault can be injected on (ASKTIME / FORMATTIME / ASSIGN, the Db2 INSERT of the PROCTRAN row, LINK DELACC).
